Playbook.name: F5 WAF — Telemetry Stopped (Log Absence) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: No F5 WAF events arrived for 15 minutes. This replaces the old inverted heartbeat (which alerted every minute logs existed). Triage question: is this a benign quiet period / maintenance, or has WAF logging (and possibly WAF protection) failed or been disabled - leaving internet banking unprotected and blind?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Loss of WAF telemetry blinds detection for the bank's internet-facing apps; if protection also dropped, exploitation could proceed unseen.

Assets.AssetType: F5 BIG-IP ASM / Advanced WAF fronting JCB internet banking and public web apps
Published banking applications and their backend servers

LogSources.LogSource: F5 ASM CEF events via syslog -> logs-cef.log-* (observer.vendor F5)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: F5 ASM logging to CEF over syslog, parsed into logs-cef.log-* (verified live).

CEF fields: deviceCustomString4=attack_type, deviceCustomNumber2=violation_rating (>=4 = real attack), deviceCustomString1=security policy, requestUrl, requestMethod, deviceCustomNumber1=HTTP response code, deviceCustomString6=source geo, cef.name=violation name, event.action=passed|alerted|blocked.

Signal.Name: F5 log absence
Signal.Details: Zero F5 events in the last 15 minutes (ES|QL COUNT == 0).

InitialAssessment.Rule: A short quiet window overnight can be benign; a sustained gap during business hours is an outage or tampering and must be escalated to the WAF/network team fast.

Investigation.Goal: Confirm whether F5 telemetry has genuinely stopped and for how long, to distinguish a brief lull from an outage/tampering.

Step.name: Confirm F5 event flow over the last 2 hours
Step.Purpose: See whether events truly stopped and when the last one arrived - a real gap vs a momentary lull.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), devices = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceHostName) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: events == 0 over 2h confirms a sustained outage. A recent last_seen (minutes ago) with a small count suggests a brief lull already recovering. deviceHostName lists which F5 units were last reporting.

Step.name: Is any CEF telemetry still flowing (pipeline vs device)
Step.Purpose: Distinguish an F5-specific outage from a whole-pipeline failure: if OTHER CEF vendors still flow, the problem is the F5 device/feed.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 30 minutes | STATS events = COUNT(*), vendors = VALUES(observer.vendor) BY observer.vendor | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: If Kaspersky/NETSCOUT/Forcepoint CEF still arrive but F5 does not, the F5 syslog feed or device is the fault (not the whole pipeline). If NOTHING arrives, it is a collector/pipeline outage.

Node.Condition: INV-01 confirms zero F5 events for a sustained period while INV-02 shows other CEF vendors still flowing.
Node.Result: True Positive (F5 Telemetry/Feed Outage - escalate to WAF/network ops; verify WAF still enforcing)

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows all CEF telemetry stopped.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (Collector/Pipeline Outage - escalate to logging ops)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows events resumed within minutes (a brief lull, e.g. low overnight traffic).
Sustained F5 gap coinciding with a change window but no confirmation it is planned.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-F5ABS-FLOW, INV-02-F5ABS-PIPELINE to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A brief, benign lull in F5 events (genuine low traffic), already recovering.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm recovery; close as benign_activity; consider widening the absence window if overnight lulls recur.

TruePositive.Definition: F5 protection/logging genuinely stopped - device down, syslog feed broken, or tampering.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the F5 units are up and ENFORCING (not just logging).
Treat internet-banking apps as temporarily unmonitored - heighten other perimeter monitoring until restored.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A logging pipeline/collector outage affecting CEF ingestion broadly.

Indicators.Item: All CEF vendors stopped, not just F5.

SOCAction.Item: Escalate to logging/SIEM ops; restore the CEF collector.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm whether the F5 units are up and enforcing.
Escalate to WAF/network or logging ops per INV-02.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Restore the F5 syslog feed or collector; verify enforcement remained active during the gap.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Add device-health monitoring on the F5 units; consider redundant log paths for the WAF feed.

QualityChecks.Check: This is an absence detection - the alert means no data, so the queries look slightly wider (2h/30m) to confirm the gap and its scope.
Suppression 2h so one outage pages once.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: F5 feed restored; enforcement confirmed active throughout; visibility gap documented.
